A 5 kg mass is attached to a horizontal spring with spring constant $k=20\text{ N/m}$ and displaced 0.4 m from equilibrium.

**(a)** Calculate the magnitude of the restoring force on the mass at this displacement.

**(b)** Calculate the period of oscillation.

**(c)** Calculate the angular frequency $\omega$, and verify that it is consistent with your answer to part (b) using $\omega = 2\pi/T$.

rubric.description: Correctly verifies ω=2π/T also gives 2 rad/s, matching part (c)'s direct calculation

prompt:
A pendulum clock needs a period of exactly 2 s to keep accurate time ($g=9.8\text{ m/s}^2$).

**(a)** Starting from the pendulum period formula, solve for the required length $L$ in terms of $T$ and $g$.

**(b)** Calculate the numerical value of $L$ needed.

**(c)** If the clock is accidentally built with a pendulum that is too long, will the period be longer or shorter than 2 s? Explain using the period formula.

rubric.description: Correctly rearranges T=2π√(L/g) to get L=g(T/2π)^2
Correctly substitutes T=2 and g=9.8 into the rearranged formula
Correctly explains that a longer pendulum has a longer period, since T is proportional to √L (an increasing function of L)

sampleResponse:
(a) Starting from T=2π√(L/g): T/(2π) = √(L/g), so (T/(2π))^2 = L/g, giving L = g(T/(2π))^2.
(b) L = (9.8)(2/(2π))^2 = (9.8)(1/π)^2 ≈ (9.8)(0.1013) ≈ 0.993 m.
(c) A pendulum that is too long will have a LONGER period than 2 s. Since T=2π√(L/g) is an increasing function of L (T grows as L grows), a larger L produces a larger T.

prompt:

**(a)** Calculate the total mechanical energy of the system.

**(b)** Calculate the maximum speed of the mass.

**(c)** Calculate the mass's kinetic energy at the moment its displacement is $x=0.2$ m.

rubric.description: Correctly computes v_max using either ωA (with ω=√(k/m)) or √(2E/m), getting 1.2 m/s
Correctly computes the potential energy at x=0.2 m: PE=(1/2)kx^2=0.36 J
Correctly uses E=KE+PE to find KE = 1.44-0.36 = 1.08 J
